confidence_notes: Five price searches returned only third-party cost-of-living index snippets (CityCost, Hikersbay, Expatistan, Jobicy and similar). These disagree by roughly 2-3x (draft beer about $2-6, inexpensive meal about $10-25, mid-range meal for two about $33-60) and are often AI-derived, thin-sample or undated. Food and drink anchors are therefore bounded mid-points leaning toward Ushuaia's remote-tourist premium, assuming roughly ARS 1,500 per USD (inferred from index currency conversions, not verified). Cocktail (about 1.7x beer) and wine glass (about 1.0x beer) are set from the local beer relationship. I found only one loose cross-check for cocktails (an index price of about $10 in a downtown club) and no restaurant by-the-glass wine price. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for a July winter/shoulder window; I ran no accommodation searches and inspected no live listings. Summer peak rates and peso volatility could move them materially.
comparable_city_reasoning: Priced from general knowledge against Argentine tourist cities (Buenos Aires, Bariloche) at the current strong-real-peso USD level, with an uplift for Ushuaia's remote, import-dependent Antarctica-gateway tourism. Accommodation is compared with other Patagonian gateway towns such as El Calafate and Bariloche in winter/shoulder season.
